energy.geoCoverageHint: % of messages with detected inference region
energy.naturalGasM3: natural gas burned by a power plant
energy.naturalGasFootnote: Volume of natural gas a modern combined-cycle gas turbine (~55 % efficiency, lower heating value ~35.8 MJ/m³ ≈ 9.94 kWh/m³) would need to burn at the plant to deliver this period's electrical energy at the data-center wall — about 0.183 m³ per kWh. Older simple-cycle peakers need ~50–60 % more.
energy.solarPanelsFootnote: Area of rooftop PV modules (~20% efficiency, 0.75 performance ratio) that, sited in {{region}}, would take exactly the selected time window to generate this period's total energy consumption. Scales with the regional annual solar irradiance and the chosen period length.
energy.windRotationsFootnote: Rotations of a typical modern 3 MW onshore wind turbine at ~15 RPM under a 35 % capacity factor — ~1.17 kWh per rotation at average output. Equivalently, one such turbine would need {{minutes}} min at its real-world average output (or {{ratedMinutes}} min at rated 3 MW) to generate your period's total energy.
energy.hydroTurbineFootnote: Volume of water that would need to pass through a typical modern hydroelectric turbine (~100 m head, ~90 % efficiency) to generate this period's energy — about 4,077 L per kWh, derived from E = m·g·h·η. High-head plants need less (Hoover Dam, 180 m: ~2,200 L/kWh); low-head run-of-river plants need much more.
energy.nuclearWasteFootnote: Engineered disposal-facility volume — not raw waste — if the same energy came from 100 % nuclear (~4 mL/kWh). Weighted blend of HLW emplacement per Posiva KBS-3 (~1,500× raw spent-fuel volume once copper canister, bentonite buffer, and thermally-spaced repository tunnels are counted — Onkalo excavates ~1 million m³ of rock for ~650 m³ of spent fuel), plus ILW (~5×) and LLW (~3×) disposal, using IAEA waste-inventory volume shares. HLW must be safely isolated and guarded for ~100,000 years before its radioactivity decays to the level of natural uranium ore.

energy.disclaimer: Estimates only — ±55% uncertainty. Anthropic does not publish per-request energy data. Not for regulatory use.
energy.noData: No energy data available for this period.

calc.title: How this is calculated
calc.intro: Every tile on this tab is derived from the token counts Anthropic's API returns for each message. Here is exactly how that token-level data becomes the kWh, kg CO₂, and equivalent figures shown above, using your actual period's numbers so you can audit the math.
calc.totals: Raw total {{raw}} kWh × PUE {{pue}} = {{totalKwh}} kWh consumed. At {{region}} grid intensity {{gridIntensity}} gCO₂/kWh, that is {{co2Kg}} kg CO₂.
calc.equivHeader: How the equivalents were derived from {{co2Kg}} kg CO₂ / {{totalKwh}} kWh:

eq.train: Long-distance train: {{co2Kg}} kg ÷ 0.006 kg CO₂/pkm = {{value}} km
eq.transit: Local transit: {{co2Kg}} kg ÷ 0.030 kg CO₂/pkm = {{value}} km
eq.nuclearWaste: Nuclear disposal volume: {{totalKwh}} kWh × 4 mL/kWh (engineered HLW+ILW+LLW repository, weighted) = {{value}}
eq.wind: Wind-turbine rotations: {{totalKwh}} kWh ÷ 1.17 kWh/rotation (3 MW turbine at 15 RPM, 35 % CF) = {{value}} rotations ≈ {{minutes}} min of real-world spinning
eq.hydro: Hydro-turbine water volume: {{totalKwh}} kWh × 4,077 L/kWh (~100 m head, 90 % η via E = m·g·h·η) = {{value}}

methodology.label: Model energy rates
methodology.value: Derived from Google's 2025 Gemini inference whitepaper (0.24 Wh/median text query) and Epoch AI 2024 token-level estimates, scaled by model class (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus). Formula details in /doc/analysis/energy-dashboard/01-estimation-model.md.

pue.label: Data-center overhead
pue.value: PUE 1.2 — Uptime Institute 2023 hyperscale average (Google, AWS, Azure publish 1.10–1.20).

gridIntensity.label: Grid carbon intensity
gridIntensity.value: US: EPA eGRID2022. EU: European Environment Agency (EEA) 2024. Asia-Pacific & global: IEA 2024. National agencies used where available.

solarYield.label: Solar panel yield
solarYield.value: Regional annual GHI from PVGIS (Europe) / NREL NSRDB (Americas) / World Bank GSA (global), multiplied by 20% panel efficiency × 0.75 performance ratio. The tile scales this annual yield down to the selected period to show the panel area required to produce exactly this period's energy in that timeframe.

windTurbine.label: Wind turbine reference
windTurbine.value: Modern 3 MW onshore turbine at 15 RPM and ~35 % capacity factor (IRENA Renewable Power Generation Costs 2023, IEA Renewables 2024). Energy per rotation = 3 MW × 4 s × 0.35 ≈ 1.17 kWh at average output (~3.33 kWh at rated).

hydroTurbine.label: Hydroelectric turbine reference
hydroTurbine.value: Representative modern hydroelectric plant at ~100 m net head with ~90 % combined turbine+generator efficiency. Derived from the physical relation E = m·g·h·η with g = 9.81 m/s², giving 3,600,000 J ÷ (9.81 × 100 × 0.9) ≈ 4,077 L/kWh. Close to the global capacity-weighted average (Three Gorges ~95 m, Itaipu ~118 m); high-head plants such as Hoover Dam (180 m) need ~2,200 L/kWh.

carKm.label: Car emissions
carKm.value: 120 gCO₂/km — EU new-car fleet average, EEA 2024.

transit.label: Local transit emissions
transit.value: 30 gCO₂/passenger-km — weighted blend of urban bus (~27), subway/metro (~8), and tram/light rail from IEA Transport Emissions (2024) and EEA Transport & Environment Reporting Mechanism 2024.

train.label: Long-distance train emissions
train.value: 6 gCO₂/passenger-km — European electrified intercity rail average, UIC Railway Handbook on Energy and CO₂ Emissions and EEA 2024.

tree.label: Tree absorption
tree.value: 21 kg CO₂ absorbed per year by a mature tree — US Forest Service / EPA.

naturalGas.label: Natural-gas power plant
naturalGas.value: Modern combined-cycle gas turbine (CCGT) at ~55 % electrical efficiency, with natural gas at lower heating value 35.8 MJ/m³ (≈ 9.94 kWh/m³). Yields ~0.183 m³ of natural gas burned per kWh of electricity delivered. Efficiency reference: IEA Electricity 2024, US EIA Annual Energy Outlook 2024.

nuclearWaste.label: Nuclear disposal volume
nuclearWaste.value: ~4 mL/kWh engineered repository volume — not raw waste. Weighted across HLW disposal per Posiva KBS-3 / Onkalo (~1,500× raw spent-fuel volume after copper canister, bentonite buffer, and thermal tunnel spacing), ILW (~5×) and LLW (~3×) disposal, using IAEA volume shares. References: Posiva 2012 safety case, SKB TR-11-01, IAEA Radioactive Waste Inventory.

backup.title: Backup & Sync
backup.intro: Back up your usage history to a folder you own — typically a consumer cloud folder (Dropbox, iCloud, Google Drive, OneDrive) — and sync it across your devices. With end-to-end encryption, data is sealed on this device before it leaves; the keys stay on your devices.
backup.notConfigured: Backup is not set up on this device.
backup.noneDetected: No cloud folder detected — enter a folder path below.
backup.encryptedHint: Everything is sealed on this device before upload. You get a recovery key — without it (or an already-connected device) the backup cannot be read.
backup.plaintextWarning: Anyone with access to the folder — including the cloud provider — can read your usage data, including prompt text.
backup.recoveryKeyPrompt: This folder already contains a claude-stats backup. Paste its recovery key to connect this device.
backup.recoveryKeyInstructions: Save this key somewhere safe, e.g. a password manager. You need it to restore your data or connect another device. It is shown only this once and cannot be recovered later.
backup.keyNotConfirmedReminder: You haven't confirmed saving your recovery key yet. Without it, an encrypted backup cannot be restored.
backup.disableConfirm: Turn off backup on this device? Files already in the backup folder are kept, and other devices are unaffected. Click again to confirm.

errors.existingBackup: This folder already contains a backup — paste its recovery key to connect this device.
errors.noBackupFound: No backup was found in that folder.
errors.wrongKey: That key didn't work. Check for typos and try again.
errors.unauthorized: Session expired — reload the page and try again.
errors.internal: Something went wrong. Check the terminal for details and try again.

pricing.title: Token Pricing (per 1M tokens)
pricing.source: Source: Anthropic API pricing — last updated {{date}} (auto-refreshed weekly). Costs shown are equivalent API rates, not subscription charges.
pricing.ttlBasisNote: Cache writes are priced at one of two rates depending on the ephemeral TTL recorded at write time — the Cache Write column (5-minute) or Cache Write (1h) (1-hour). A jump between them on the same workload is this basis switching, not a pricing error — see the Cache TTL fit below the plan panel.

verdict.prefer5m: The 5-minute cache TTL would cost about {{money}} less over this window.
verdict.prefer1h: The 1-hour cache TTL would cost about {{money}} less over this window.
verdict.tooClose: The two cache TTLs cost about the same over this window (difference: {{money}}) — not worth switching.
verdict.insufficientData: Not enough cache-TTL data yet in this window to recommend a setting.

byModel.title: Per-model net cost of the short TTL
byModel.unpriced: Excludes {{count}} unpriced rows ({{tokens}} cache-write tokens) — no model, or no rate for this model.

margin.title: Margin
margin.nearBoundary: Near-boundary band ({{minutes}} min just under the short TTL): {{requests}} requests, {{readTokens}} cache-read tokens
margin.impliedSwing: Implied swing if this band also expired

contextCarry.title: Context carry
contextCarry.distinctClause: The average request carried about {{carried}} tokens of context to produce about {{distinct}} tokens of new content.
contextCarry.distinctUnavailable: Not enough data this window to estimate how much of each request's context was new versus carried forward.
contextCarry.biasNote: This estimate is biased in both directions: content that is dropped and re-read later is counted as new a second time, while a post-reset baseline is counted as new even though it may only be a summary of what was dropped.
contextCarry.carryCostLabel: Carry cost (lower bound — priced at the cache-read rate)

sawtooth.title: Reset shape
sawtooth.line: Context resets to about {{floor}} tokens, then climbs to about {{peak}} before the next reset, over about {{cycle}} requests per cycle.
sawtooth.insufficientData: Fewer than 3 resets in this window — not enough to describe a shape.

aboveCap.title: Tokens carried above a cap
aboveCap.caveat: Tokens above a cap are priced at the cache-read rate — the cheapest form this cost can take, and a lower bound on it. This is not the cost of capping context at that level: capping means the same work gets done with less context in front of the model, and what that rework costs is not measured here.

modelTierWaste.title: Route simpler prompts to cheaper models
modelTierWaste.body: {{overusePercent}}% of your classified turns were sent to a pricier model than their complexity warranted. Check the Efficiency section to see which prompts drove the overspend and consider using Haiku/Sonnet for the simpler ones.

planUnderusing.title: Consider downgrading to {{plan}}
planUnderusing.body: Your average API-equivalent usage is only ~{{monthlyUse}}/mo — well below your current ~{{monthlyFee}}/mo plan fee. Downgrading would still cover your typical usage.

contextCompaction.title: Use /compact or /clear more aggressively
contextCompaction.body: {{count}} long sessions (15+ prompts) ran without compaction. Long uncompacted contexts re-send the entire history each turn, inflating input-token cost. Start a new conversation or run /compact for unrelated tasks.

cacheLowHitRate.title: Cache hit rate is low — restructure prompts
cacheLowHitRate.body: Only {{percent}}% of your input tokens hit the prompt cache. Keeping a stable prefix (system prompt, tool definitions, long context) at the start of each turn lets Anthropic reuse it at ~10% the price of fresh input tokens.

runawayConversation.title: One conversation is dominating your spend
runawayConversation.body: Session in {{project}} cost {{cost}} across {{promptCount}} prompts — {{ratio}}× the median session. Long single conversations grow their own context on every turn; consider splitting unrelated work into fresh sessions.

contextNearLimit.title: Sessions are regularly filling the context window
contextNearLimit.body: Your average peak input reaches ~{{thousands}}k tokens (out of a 200k ceiling). Near-full contexts are slower and more expensive per turn, and further prompts risk truncation. Run /compact earlier — or start a fresh session once a task is complete.

mcpHeavy.title: MCP server “{{server}}” is consuming an unusually large share
mcpHeavy.body: {{sharePercent}}% of your total spend (~{{cost}}) went to this server across {{calls}} calls, averaging {{avgTokens}} tokens per call{{medianClause}}. Verify that it is returning the right amount of data and not looping or echoing large payloads.

goodCache.title: Excellent cache discipline
goodCache.body: {{percent}}% of your input tokens are coming from the prompt cache — strong reuse of stable prefixes is saving you real money on every turn.

goodModelRouting.title: You're picking the right model for the job
goodModelRouting.body: Only {{overusePercent}}% of your classified turns used a pricier model than needed. You're matching prompt complexity to model tier well.

goodPlanValue.title: Great value from your plan
goodPlanValue.body: Your API-equivalent usage averages ~{{multiplier}}× your plan fee. The subscription is paying for itself several times over.

goodCompaction.title: Good context hygiene
goodCompaction.body: {{percent}}% of your sessions show compaction activity, and few long sessions went uncompacted. You're keeping context sizes in check.
